entity.name: Thalha Ahmed
entity.description: Developer from India who builds open source OSINT and security tools. I wrote and maintain Helix on my own: the engine, the site checks, the releases on PyPI, Docker, BlackArch and the AUR, and the daily public status page.

projects.name: Helix
projects.description: Helix checks a username across about 12,000 sites and re-checks every account it finds against made-up usernames before reporting it, so a site that says yes to any name cannot produce a false result. Every site is tested once a day against a real account and a made-up name, with the results on a public status page. Results are graded for how likely the accounts belong to one person and can be sealed with a fingerprint so anyone can verify later that nothing was edited. It also shows people their own footprint with a delete link for each account, and watches a username over time. Runs on the user's own machine: no account, no telemetry. Built for investigators, journalists and security researchers, and for ordinary people checking what is public about them.

plans.name: One year of Helix development
plans.description: One year of part-time work, paid by milestone: publish an open accuracy test on real accounts against Sherlock, Maigret and Blackbird; raise the share of sites that answer above 95% with zero false positives; ship Helix inside Trace, Maltego and SpiderFoot; get the translations checked by native speakers; keep the daily site check, releases and packages running. Progress posted on GitHub every quarter.
